subject: reasoning
question:
Refer to the following number and symbol series and answer the question that follows (all numbers are single-digit numbers only). Counting to be done from left to right only.

(Left) 1 5 7 8 = 6 9 2 + 5 7 3 % 7 8 $ 4 1 5 # 8 @ & 4 9 6 (Right)

How many such symbols are there, each of which is immediately preceded by an odd number and also immediately followed by an even number?
solution:
**Given: **(Left) 1 5 7 8 = 6 9 2 + 5 7 3 % 7 8 $ 4 1 5 # 8 @ & 4 9 6 (Right)

Now,

Symbols, each of which is immediately preceded by an odd number and also immediately followed by an even number.

So, the needed pattern is: Odd Number — Symbol — Even Number

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d5737756501cecccefc7edee2af11bc35586b2347a451c48ff7a23a26e2f480d.png] Thus, there is one such symbol, each of which is immediately preceded by an odd number and also immediately followed by an even number.

Hence, the correct answer is "**Option 3**".
